name: CONUS / CONUS+
notes: One-experiment-record decision (per WAVE3_LEAD_BRIEF.md): the CONUS+ overview paper (arXiv:2407.11912) states CONUS+ is 'continuing on this way the CONUS physics program started at the Brokdorf nuclear power plant' using 'the same four point-contact high-purity germanium (HPGe) detectors produced for the former experiment, however refurbished'. This is the same collaboration, same detector array, relocated to a new reactor site under a new name; recorded as one experiment:conus record, not two lineage-linked records.

'CONUS+' is not encoded as a formal `aliases` entry: the validator's A20 duplicate-name check strips non-alphanumeric characters before comparing, so 'CONUS+' normalises to the same string as the name 'CONUS' and is rejected as a redundant alias ('alias equal to own name'). The name/alias relationship is documented here in prose instead.
No INSPIRE experiment-registry record was found for CONUS/CONUS+ (searched inspirehep.net/api/experiments this session; zero results); external.inspire_experiment left null rather than guessed.
links.website is null: no official CONUS/CONUS+ website was found reachable in this pass (attempts at plausible MPIK URLs returned 404); this is a gap, not a considered absence.

Record name is 'CONUS / CONUS+' (not just 'CONUS') so that the in-app search, which matches only `name`/`aliases` (never `summary`), surfaces this experiment when a user searches 'CONUS+'. 'CONUS+' cannot be a formal alias (A20 rejects it as equal to the name modulo punctuation), and the collaboration/detector records already use this same 'X / X+' convention, so the experiment record is changed to match them for consistency and discoverability. [verifier fix, 2026-09-17]

physics_goals.quote: The CONUS+ experiment aims to detect coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CEvNS) of reactor antineutrinos on germanium nuclei in the fully coherent regime
physics_goals.value: Detect and precisely measure CEvNS of reactor antineutrinos on germanium nuclei in the fully coherent regime

summary.plain: A small, sensitive detector using ultra-pure germanium crystals to catch reactor antineutrinos gently bouncing off whole atomic nuclei, first run at a German nuclear plant and, after it closed, moved to a Swiss one under the name CONUS+.
summary.technical: Reactor CEvNS experiment using an array of four 1 kg point-contact HPGe spectrometers; ran as CONUS at the Brokdorf nuclear power plant, Germany (17.1 m baseline, 3.9 GWth core, 2018-2023), then relocated as CONUS+ to the Leibstadt nuclear power plant, Switzerland (20.7 m baseline, 3.6 GWth core, from November 2023), reporting a first direct 3.7σ observation of reactor CEvNS in January 2025.
